div.head: V As Prol.
div.ab: Æðelstan cyng cyþ: þæt ic hæbbe geahsod, þæt ure frið is wyrs gehealden, ðonne me lyste oþþe hit æt Greatanlea gecweden wære; ⁊ mina witan secgað, þæt ic hit to lange forboren hæbbe.
Ic Æthelstan cyng cyþ, þæt ic hæbbe geacsod, þæt ure fryþ is wyrs gehealden, ðonne me lyst, oþþe hit æt Greatanlæge gecwæden wære; ⁊ mine witan secgaþ, þæt ic hit to long forboren hæbbe.

Decretum Æthelstani de pace obseruanda. Ego Æthelstanus rex notifico uobis, sicut accepi (innotuit mihi), quod pax nostra peius obseruata est, quam michi placeat uel apud Greateleiam fuerit institutum, et sapientes mei dicunt, quod hoc diutius pertuli quam debueram.
Æðelstan cyng cyþ, þæt ic hæbbe geahsod, þæt ure frið is wyrs gehealden ðonne me lyste, oþþe hit æt Greatanlea gecweden wære; ⁊ mina witan secgað, þæt ic hit to lange forboren hæbbe.

Prolog. Ich, König Aethelstan, verkünde (-det H): dass ich erfahren habe, dass unser Friede schlechter gewahrt wird als mir gefällt oder [als] es zu Greatley bestimmt worden ist; und meine Witan sagen, dass ich das zu lange geduldet habe.

Prologue. I, King Æthelstan, make known (makes known, H): that I have learned that our peace is kept worse than pleases me or [than] was determined at Greatley; and my witan say that I have put up with it too long.

I, King Æthelstan, declare that I have learned that the public peace has not been kept to the extent, either of my wishes, or of the provisions laid down at Grately. And my councillors say that I have suffered this too long.
I, King Athelstan, make known that I have learnt that our peace is worse kept than I should like and than it was pronounced at Grately; and my councillors say that I have borne it too long.
div.note: Base text (K) is Ld (Lambarde 1568), f. 61. In H it follows II As after a paragraph break, without heading; Liebermann thinks ‘Ic Æ. c. cyðe’ (as Ld, Quadr.) was probably the archetype. note.seg: ‘Ich der König’ beginnen auch Ine, Af El 49, 9, I As, As Alm, dagegen in dritter Person I. II Ew. I. II Em und Spätere. Um so mehr scheint Ic in lq archetyp
Ine, Af El 49, 9, I As and As Alm also begin ‘I the king’, whereas I. II Ew, I. II Em and later laws use the third person. All the more does Ic seem to be archetypal in lq
In Ld ist hinter cyð das -e wie oft ausgefallen, vielleicht weil in der späten Hs. abgekürzt und vom Drucker übersehen
In Ld the -e after cyð has dropped out, as often happens, perhaps because it was abbreviated in the late MS and overlooked by the printer
Ähnlich beginnt mit Klage über ungenügende polizeiliche Sicherheit II Ew 1; vgl. Gl Frieden 1 a
II Ew 1 begins similarly with a complaint about inadequate public security; cf. Gl Frieden 1 a
Nicht II As 20, 3 besonders, sondern das ganze Gesetz scheint gemeint
What seems to be meant is not II As 20, 3 in particular but the whole law
Diese Initiative der Witan ist selten; vgl. Gl Gesetz 15 d; mein National assembly p. 67
This initiative on the part of the witan is rare; cf. Gl Gesetz 15 d; my National assembly p. 67
The reference (Grately) is to II As.

This code illustrates Athelstan’s readiness to take strong measures to prevent defiance of the law and corruption among judges. It survives in Textus Roffensis and in Nowell’s transcript of Cott. Otho B. xi, and in Quadripartitus. Though cited as V Athelstan, it preceded the codes cited as III and IV Athelstan. It is edited by Liebermann, 1, 166–9; and with English translation by Attenborough, pp. 152–8, Thorpe, 1, 220–5.
